newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-NO CHARITY FOR UNITED FROM DETERMINED JUVE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NO CHARITY FOR UNITED FROM DETERMINED JUVE.

text.p: Italian champions Juventus have warned Champions' League opponents Manchester United that they are not in England on a mercy mission in Wednesday's vital clash.
Juve are all but mathematically assured of a place in the last eight of Europe's premier competition and have half an eye on their World Club Championship clash with Argentina's River Plate in Tokyo.
Additionally, if they were to finish second in Group C rather than top, they would avoid an almost certain quarter-final clash with arch-rivals and compatriots AC Milan.
But any hopeful souls in Manchester counting on a half-hearted approach from the European champions, in a game from which United must take at least a point, are in for a rude shock.

"I am aiming for the best possible side I can field," Juventus coach Marcelo Lippi promised when the club arrived this week. "We play in the World Club Championship in Tokyo next week but I can assure everyone that we will not play with that game on our minds."
United's 19-year-old defender Philip Neville takes Lippi at his word.
"Anyone who thinks that Juventus will not try too hard to win the group because they don't want to come up against AC Milan in the next round can forget it," he said. "That is rubbish."
"They've proved they are the team to beat in Europe. It will take a great performance to beat them. We admire them, they have got good players and we will have to play to our peak to beat them."
United will enter the match at Old Trafford still haunted by memories of their historic home defeat by Fenerbahce in their last European clash there three weeks ago.
On that occasion is was a Bosnian sharp-shooter, Elvir Bolic, who undid United. On Wednesday it could well be a Croat.

Alen Boksic, the Croatian international United tried to sign last seaosn, has scored four out of eight goals for Juventus in the competition so far, including the one that sunk United 1-0 in Turin in September.
He will relish a second chance to exploit United's achilles heel this season -- the centre of their defence.

United's David May and Ronny Johnsen have struggled to emulate the rock-solid partnership of Steve Bruce -- who left Old Trafford in the summer -- and the injured Gary Pallister, while the Neville brothers are still establishing themselves on the flanks.

"People forget that we've changed the whole back four in the space of two years," explained United boss Alex Ferguson this week. "I don't know many teams who could handle that. Bruce and Pallister were the foundation for this club to be successful, absolutely no doubt about that."

On the positive side for Ferguson, Ryan Giggs returns on the left to lend balance to a side woefully out of sorts over the last month, and Ireland international Roy Keane is also available after suspension.

For Juve, who enter the match on the back of a 0-0 draw with Milan at the weekend and a 3-0 Italian Cup defeat against Internazionale, central defenders Paolo Montero of Uruguay and Ciro Ferrara are likely to return.
They were suspended for the Milan match, but are now set to oust Mark Juliano and Alessio Tacchinardi from Lippi's starting side.

Gifted playmaker Alessandro Del Piero, who came on as an 85th minute substitute against Milan, may again be sacrificed for a 4-4-2 line-up in which Boksic will be partnered by either Michele Padovano or Christian Vieri.

If United lose their second home European tie in 40 years, to compound their disastrous result against Fenerbahce, they would then have to go to Rapid Vienna and win, and still rely on Juve beating the Turkish champions in Turin.
Faced with that prospect, United will be hoping for a helping hand from history. The Italians have won only once in nine visits to England -- against Aston Villa in the 1982-83 European Cup.
